interview_sample.note: Example data: an invented paid search agency and an invented dental practice, not real businesses. Every number in interview_output follows from this input.
interview_sample.request: Hey Claude, I just added the "case-study-writer" skill. Write a customer story from this interview with the practice manager at Example Family Dental, our client since June. Their form answers and the transcript are below. They said we can check the numbers in the Google Ads account we manage for them.
interview_sample.brand: Example Growth Agency (invented), a paid search agency for dental and medical clinics
interview_sample.stage: stage 3 (form answers and transcript supplied); the stage 1 request and stage 2 form were sent earlier and are shown as they were drafted
interview_sample.permission_reply: Happy to do it. Practice and my role only, please, and I want to see the quotes before anything goes out.
interview_sample.typical_results: unknown: the agency has no figure for what its dental clients generally get

form_answers.F1: Booked new patients who chose 'Google ad' as how they found us, from the referral-source report in our practice software.
form_answers.F4: The agency took over our Google Ads on 2026-06-01. New campaigns and call tracking were live by 2026-06-20, so we left June out.
form_answers.F5: We opened Saturday mornings at one location from 2026-08-01. No price changes. Same front desk team.
form_answers.F6: A family dental practice with 3 locations in the US Midwest, 11 dentists and hygienists.
form_answers.F7: Name the practice and my role (practice manager), not my name. The logo is fine.
form_answers.F8: One month of management fees was waived for taking part in this story.
form_answers.F9: Yes, check the Google Ads account you manage for us.
form_answers.F10: Our Google Ads spend, from the monthly invoices.
form_answers.F12: About $6,000 a month, the same budget, 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Walk me through a normal week before you started with the agency.

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: Every Monday I'd open the Google Ads bill and have no idea what we got for it. The phones rang, but nobody could tell me which calls came from the ads.

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: Mostly time and nerves. I spent Friday afternoons trying to match invoices to new patient forms, and I still couldn't say if the money worked.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What made you start looking, and why then?

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: We were about to open Saturdays and I didn't want to spend more on ads I couldn't measure. Another practice owner told me she finally knew her cost per new patient.

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: Switching agencies felt risky in our busy season. We agreed to keep the same budget so the only thing changing was how it was run.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What did the first month look like?

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: June was messy. The call tracking numbers went in, the front desk had to learn to ask how people found us, and we paused the old campaigns for a week.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Take the numbers on your form. How do you know them?

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: The booked patients come straight from our practice software, the referral-source report. Honestly, it cut our cost per new patient in half.

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: Implant enquiries are still slow. We haven't seen much change there. And I'd guess our phones get twenty more calls a week, but I haven't counted.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell a practice like yours that's about to start?

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: Fix your tracking before you judge any agency. Once the front desk asked every caller how they found us, the reports finally matched what we saw in the chairs.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Is there anything you said today that should stay off the record?

transcript.speaker: Practice manager
transcript.text: Off the record, our old agency never once sent us a report. Please leave that out.

connected_pull.query: SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name, segments.date, metrics.impressions, metrics.clicks, metrics.cost_micros, metrics.conversions FROM campaign WHERE segments.date BETWEEN '<START>' AND '<END>' ORDER BY segments.date LIMIT 5000
connected_pull.account: the practice's Google Ads account, managed by the agency (invented id 1234567890)
connected_pull.rows: summed across the 5 campaigns per day; cost in dollars (cost_micros / 1,000,000)
